correctness.rationale: The exact integer potential \(b=(d-1)s-c-a\) is nondecreasing under both types of stacking, including all root-simplex cases and the first deleted vertex when no original vertex is deleted. For every nonempty cut \(S\), this proves \(\omega(G-S)\le(d-1)|S|-(d-2)\). The Kleetope of a stacked polytope with \(N\) original vertices has exactly \((d-1)N-(d-2)(d+1)\) independent new vertices after the \(N\) original vertices are deleted, so its upper toughness ratio tends to \(1/(d-1)\). Since \(d-2>0\), the finite-graph lower bound is strict. A standalone standard-library checker completed 35,816 exhaustive small-graph cut checks and 32 exact Kleetope checks; the universal conclusion uses the induction, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The result gives the exact best possible positive toughness threshold \(1/(d-1)\) for stacked convex polytopes of every dimension \(d\ge4\), even though the motivating 2026 theorem shows no positive uniform threshold for the larger class of simplicial polytopes. A monotone exposed-facet budget explains why the recursively stacked class is different, and the explicit Kleetope family proves sharpness. This is a structural infinite-family comparison rather than a finite computation.
